title: Tenant header shadowing caused billing divergence during hybrid routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported unexpected monthly invoice deltas (up to +17%) after we enabled hybrid routing for traffic steering between Hosted and Dedicated pools. Investigation shows certain requests routed through hybrid paths had tenant attribution lost or overwritten when an X-Tenant-Candidate header was present from an upstream proxy. This led to a subset of tokens being attributed to a shadow tenant ID and excluded from the canonical tenant rollups used for billing reconciliation. Scope: Affects requests that satisfy all of: (1) traverse hybrid routing policy (fallback to dedicated pool), (2) include upstream proxy headers (X-Tenant-*, X-Forwarded-Client), and (3) hit the edge proxy during a routing table reload window. Impacted customers: 3 enterprise customers reported materially different invoices (customers anonymized in internal report). Immediate priority due to potential financial and contractual SLA implications.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Enable hybrid routing with fallback rules between hosted/dedicated in staging.
2) Send a burst of requests with header X-Tenant-Candidate set to a benign value while simultaneously triggering a routing table reload (simulate autoscaler rotation).
3) Observe that the edge middleware sometimes persists X-Tenant-Candidate into downstream request context and the metering service consumes 'tenant_id' from request context rather than authenticated token.
4) Reconcile tokens: metering rows show split counts for original tenant and shadow tenant.
Repro rate: ~15% of requests during reload window in our staging setup.
root_cause: During the hybrid-routing rollout we introduced a path where the edge proxy writes provisional routing metadata into request headers (X-Tenant-Candidate) so the orchestrator can decide eviction targets. A subsequent refactor in the metering ingestion pipeline changed the attribute precedence: when both an authenticated tenant claim and an incoming X-Tenant-* header exist, the ingestion code incorrectly favored headers for attribution. Additionally, a race during routing table reload caused older header values to be reused for new connections (connection pooling edge case). Together these caused deterministic but rare misattribution of token counts to non-canonical tenant IDs.
mitigation_and_fix: Short-term mitigation (completed 2026-03-02): 1) Turned off writing X-Tenant-Candidate at the edge for hosted/dedicated hybrid flows. 2) Temporarily enabled conservative routing (no fallback) for affected customers. Medium-term fix (implemented in PR): 1) Change metering ingestion to strictly prefer authenticated tenant claims (Authorization token) and ignore X-Tenant-* headers unless explicitly validated by the orchestrator. 2) Add defensive copy semantics to edge proxy header handling to avoid stale header reuse on pooled connections. 3) Add unit/integration tests that emulate routing reload races and header reuse. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8124 (metering: enforce tenant precedence + edge header pool fix).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR and run full integration test in 'hybrid-staging' (complete). 2) Canary rollout to non-critical customers with traffic-slice=1% for 24 hours, monitor attribution metrics and billing diffs. 3) Expand to 10% slice for 48 hours if no regressions. 4) Full rollout to all regions and re-enable X-Tenant-Candidate logic only behind an opt-in feature flag for customers that require it. 5) For affected customers, run a one-time reconciliation backfill to reassign token counts and issue bill adjustments (coord with finance).
monitoring_and_metrics: New dashboards added: 1) 'tenant_attribution_mismatch_rate' per-region per-routing-policy (Grafana panel). 2) 'shadow_tenant_token_count' time series for top 50 shadow IDs. 3) Alert: >0.1% attribution_mismatch over 1h triggers P0. Added SLO check to compare canonical tenant rollups against raw ingest every 10 minutes. Linked dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/tenant-attribution
